title: Marches at the dance halls and treating the ladies
summary: Marches at Hope Hall and Co-operators Hall: couples marched to the table where men bought fruit and sweets, and musicians sometimes skipped the march to catch non-payers.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, I think what I've heard about those is that we always forget to ask people, like Gettysburg March, they tell us they used to use that a lot to start up. Was that just an ordinary dance?
Did they do that, say, at the Economy Hall or the Operators Hall? Every hall, everybody.

The Operators Hall? Yeah, the Corporators. Now, before the Corporators, well, it was the Hope Hall. That's what my grandfather laid out at the Hope Hall. So you could have them big halls like that, you know, and they'd play them marches. When did they play that?
The very beginning of the dance, or what?

No, well, they would play them in the set. They'd play by the Foxtrot and the Waltz, and they'd play a fast and two-step, then they would play a march. Oh, and then they would march them up. Then some fellow would come in, we'd kind of cheat. Wouldn't have no money, well, the musician would watch him. And sometimes they'd skip the march, to be sure that they'd catch the fellow that duck in the march, the man that would come up at a march. So that we'd get him that he'd have to march up there and buy the lady something. So they had apples there, you know, and so forth like that, and cake, candy, and pop, and so forth.
In the march, they would march past the table?
They'd have to march up and buy something.
And they'd buy something off the table. That's right.

And sometimes they had the older folk come there with them to the dance, as chef on them, you know. But sometimes he'd call a mother, well, he'd go by the mother or something. The father that he'd buy them something. We didn't march down. Much different from mine. Yeah.
When they marched, they just sort of walked past?

Well, they'd hold hands. When the band went, da-da-da-da-da-da-da, da-da, any kind of a march. And they marched right on up there with the escort. Then they had about three or four at the table, just serving whatever they wanted. And they had to get the lady what she wanted. But she may want the pop, she may want the apple, she may want the orange. And every time she'd get it, she may don't eat it. But she'd give it to her mother. And sometimes the mother would bring a basket. Sometimes she'd come back home with a basket full of fruit. And they'd go ahead and borrow.
I never knew they did all that. Yeah.
It was very nice, let me tell you. Very nice.
